tldr: Headlines across 12 country buckets unanimously frame the Kushner shuttle as a double failure — no deal with Hamas in Cairo, no breakthrough with Netanyahu in Jerusalem — but the advertised sub-story diverges sharply: Fox News converts stalemate into a 'stark ultimatum' suggesting US resolve, wire services and the Straits Times pivot to the Israeli airstrike the following day, and Turkey's Daily Sabah is alone in headlining Hamas's counter-narrative that Israel, not Hamas, is the obstacle to a deal.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline to convert diplomatic failure into an ultimatum narrative — pairing 'stark ultimatum' with 'finish the job' — advertising the same stalemate as US resolve rather than breakdown.
The only headline to foreground Hamas's counter-narrative in the title itself, making Israel the stalling party — an attribution entirely absent from every other outlet's title layer.

The only headline to lead with the reconstruction angle ('US issues Hamas Gaza construction ultimatum'), making US economic leverage over Gaza visible at the title layer where all others focused on disarmament talks.

The only headline to pair ongoing Israeli strikes explicitly with Kushner's diplomatic visit in the title itself, foregrounding the simultaneous bombing-while-negotiating contradiction before any click.

bottom_line: At the headline layer the Kushner shuttle is universally a story of failed diplomacy, but the pre-click reason for failure is packaged differently by political lean: US right-wing media advertise strength and an ultimatum, wire services and Asian outlets show the airstrike that followed the talks, and Turkey's Daily Sabah makes Israel the named obstacle — three incompatible narratives built from the same underlying events.
